reason: Conversation 1 asked the sensible first-step questions (temperatures, can-you-keep-your-hand-on-it, smell, tripping, scorching), confirmed 4C/-18C, and correctly concluded the pattern is 'normal condenser heat' with clear stop conditions, plus a reasonable manual-clearance check and installer/retailer route; it never pushed an engineer or part. Its one notable flaw is the stray 'switch it off and unplug it' instruction in turn two, which was unjustified and confused the homeowner, though it promptly corrected this. Conversation 2 gave a good initial reassurance but then repeatedly labelled the situation 'inadequate ventilation causing overheating of condenser coils', asserted '1cm is generally not enough' without the model data, invoked speculative 'safety cut-outs', never asked about temperatures or a warm plug, and gave three near-identical answers, so it ended up over-diagnosing a fault that the ground truth says does not exist.
